title: Discovery-to-brief in 15 minutes
steps: Get the customer's consent before recording, then record with a notetaker your company has approved (e.g. Fathom, Granola). If there is no recording, use your typed notes.
Paste the transcript into your AI tool with the 'deal summary' prompt.
Ask it to list every assumption not stated by the customer.
Fix gaps with the user, then generate a 5-bullet brief for the AE and a follow-up email draft (use the second prompt). Do not send the email.
The user logs the brief in CRM and sets next-step dates.

title: Account research before first call
steps: Ask the user to paste the company's public info (site pages, latest 10-K or press releases) and the attendees' titles. If you have web access, you may read public pages yourself; cite the URL for every fact. Do not scrape LinkedIn.
Summarize business model, recent changes and likely priorities. Label every inferred pain or priority HYPOTHESIS.
Generate 10 discovery questions ranked by importance.
Flag 3 'not a fit' signals to watch for.
Return a one-page call plan with these sections: business model, recent changes, likely pains (hypotheses), 10 ranked questions, 3 not-a-fit signals, open questions.

title: Tailored demo in an hour
steps: List the top 3 pains from discovery.
Prompt the demo-story template to map pain → feature → outcome.
Generate fake but realistic demo data as CSV; the user loads it into their sandbox.
Run the 'pre-mortem my demo' prompt as the skeptical buyer.
Suggest the user record a 3-minute walkthrough (e.g. Loom) for async stakeholders.

title: POC scope that gets signed
steps: Draft the scope with the POC prompt (objective, criteria, timeline, owners).
Pressure-test each success criterion for measurability.
Review with the champion; agree on pass/fail before kickoff.
Turn the timeline into a shared checklist with dates.
Draft a recap email confirming criteria in writing for the user to review and send.

title: Agent POC with evals
steps: Pick one narrow task and collect 20–50 real example inputs (with permission).
Build the first version with an agent framework (e.g. LangGraph, OpenAI Agents SDK).
Write expected outputs and pass/fail checks for each input (first prompt), then run them through an eval tool (e.g. promptfoo, now part of OpenAI and still MIT open source, or DeepEval).
Trace failures with an observability tool (e.g. Langfuse, now part of ClickHouse and still open source, or LangSmith).
Report pass rate against the agreed criteria with the second prompt, not vibes. A zero-tolerance check that fails means the POC fails, whatever the average.

title: Security questionnaire first pass
steps: Gather your approved security docs (SOC 2 summary, DPA, architecture).
Prompt the AI to answer only from those docs and mark gaps NEEDS REVIEW.
Route NEEDS REVIEW items to security/legal owners.
Store final, approved answers in your RFP tool (e.g. Loopio, or Responsive, formerly RFPIO) for reuse.
Track turnaround time per questionnaire.

title: Integration debugging loop
steps: Reproduce the issue and capture logs, request/response and environment. Redact tokens, API keys, passwords and personal data before pasting anything into an AI tool.
Paste logs into the triage prompt for ranked root causes.
The user tests the top hypothesis with Postman, curl or a small script, and pastes the result back.
Document the fix as a runbook entry.
Share a plain-English summary with the customer.

title: 30-60-90 implementation plan
steps: Feed scope, team size and success criteria into the 30-60-90 prompt.
Generate a risk register and add customer-specific risks.
Ask the user for customer-side owners for every dependency; write TBD where none is given.
The user reviews the plan in the kickoff meeting and gets explicit agreement.
Turn milestones into weekly status-update headings.

title: Weekly status update on autopilot
steps: Keep a running notes doc per customer during the week.
Friday: paste notes into the status prompt (RAG status, done, next, blockers).
Check every owner and date is real.
Return the email as a draft. The user sends it and pins it in the shared channel.
Escalate any red item with the escalation prompt the same day.

title: Runbook from Slack chaos
steps: Export the relevant thread(s). Remove tokens, passwords and customer personal data first.
Prompt the AI to produce a numbered runbook with checks and rollback.
Follow the runbook yourself once on a test environment.
Fix steps that fail, then publish to your wiki.
Link the runbook in future tickets.

title: Deal debrief → product feedback
steps: After win/loss, paste notes into the debrief prompt.
Extract product gaps. Use only verbatim quotes that appear in the notes; if a gap has no quote, say so.
Group gaps by theme and deal size.
The user shares the gap list with product monthly in a single doc.
The user tracks which gaps ship and tells the customer.

title: EBR deck in an afternoon
steps: Export usage metrics and outcomes for the period.
Prompt the EBR outline using only the provided numbers.
Ask the user for one real customer story; take one adoption gap from the data. Mark anything missing [NEEDED].
Propose a specific next step grounded in the data; for commercial expansion, use the user's option and pricing, never invented numbers.
Rehearse with the champion before the exec meeting.
